title: Spark's Curators are execution agents with no discretion — every action must be pre-approved by a governance poll
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.9.2 states the framework's purpose as defining "the conditions under which Spark governance may authorize external contributors to **execute** approved changes onchain, while preserving governance oversight, timelock protections, and cancellation authorities." The scope clause is categorical: "Curators may only execute actions that have been explicitly approved by Spark governance via polling" (A.6.1.1.1.3.9.3.2), and A.6.1.1.1.3.9.4.1 repeats that all curator-executed changes "must be approved **in advance**."

A Curator is defined (A.6.1.1.1.3.9.3.1) as "a specific admin role defined within the Morpho smart contract system" — and this is where the design becomes interesting. In Morpho's own model, a curator is an active manager: it selects markets, sets allocation caps, and adjusts risk in response to conditions, which is the entire value proposition of a curated vault. Spark takes the contract role and strips the discretion out of it.

What remains is a division of labour. Governance retains every decision; the Curator supplies the operational capability — key custody, transaction construction, monitoring, availability — that a token-holder vote cannot itself provide. The Artifact is delegating *hands*, not judgment.

The trade-off is real. A vault whose parameters can only change at the speed of a governance poll cannot respond to a fast-moving market the way a discretionary curator can, and the Artifact accepts that cost in exchange for a mandate an observer can verify: every curator transaction should map to a specific prior poll, which is exactly what the reporting requirement forces the Curator to demonstrate.

It also means the Curator's misalignment risk is bounded to *unauthorized* action rather than *bad* action — a much easier thing to detect, and the thing the timelock and guardian exist to catch.
description: The framework separates deciding from signing: governance approves changes in advance and the Curator may only submit the corresponding transactions, inverting Morpho's usual active-management
